reason: The section allows unanimously approved necessary work despite a sufficient petition against it.

evidenceText: the council may by by-law passed by unanimous vote of the whole council

proposedGroups.reason: The target states when council may proceed despite an opposition petition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how unanimous council approval can authorize necessary or requisite work despite a sufficient petition against the proposed work.

reason: The section governs water or sewerage work ordered under the Health Act, including notice and authority despite opposition.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Health Act ordered water or sewerage work
proposedGroups.reason: All subsections address notice for ordered work and authority to proceed despite a petition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the notice and by-law process for Health Act ordered water or sewerage work and when council may proceed despite opposition.

reason: The section addresses filing, sufficiency, co-owner treatment, and withdrawal limits for petitions about work.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Work petition filing sufficiency and withdrawal
proposedGroups.reason: All subsections govern petitions for or against work.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how petitions for or against work are filed, how the clerk determines sufficiency, how co-owners count, and when names cannot be withdrawn.

reason: Section 127 separates general metre-frontage assessment from domestic sewer and water main assessment rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Metre frontage assessment and owners portion
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set default special assessment by metre frontage and owners’ portion by-law authority.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the default metre-frontage basis for assessing local improvement work and the by-law power to prescribe the owners’ portion of cost.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Domestic sewer outlet assessments and exemptions
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections govern outlet sewer exemptions, later connected parcel assessments, roll additions, and sewer account credits.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how domestic sewer outlet exemptions and later special frontage assessments for connected parcels are handled.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Water main supply assessments and exemptions
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections govern water main exemptions, later connected parcel assessments, roll additions, and water supply account credits.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how water main exemptions and later special frontage assessments for connected parcels are handled.

reason: The section is a focused assessment rule for sidewalk or curbing work.

evidenceText: Where the work undertaken is a sidewalk or curbing

proposedGroups.reason: The target states which abutting parcels are assessed and when both sides may bear sidewalk cost.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how special frontage assessment applies to sidewalk or curbing work and when both sides of the street may bear sidewalk cost.

reason: The section is a focused estimate and instalment rule for special frontage assessments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Special frontage assessment estimate and instalments
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address estimating cost, fixing instalments, and equal annual payment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how council estimates work cost, fixes annual instalments, and requires equal annual payment of the owners’ portion of cost.

reason: Section 130 separates frontage assessment reductions from municipal payment and the clerk’s reduction role.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set actual metre frontage as default and describe lot reductions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when abutting parcels are assessed by actual metre frontage and how reductions are made for corner, irregular, unfit, or double-abutting lots.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal payment and clerk reduction role
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state who pays for reductions and that the clerk makes them.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that assessment reductions are paid by the municipality, entered on the roll, and made by the clerk.

reason: The section states one formula for total metre frontage of abutting parcels to be assessed.

evidenceText: The total metre frontage of the abutting parcels to be assessed shall be determined

proposedGroups.reason: The target defines total metre frontage using reduced and actual metre frontages.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how total metre frontage is calculated for abutting parcels subject to special frontage assessment.

reason: The section states one calculation for the special frontage assessment rate.

evidenceText: The rate of a special frontage assessment shall be determined by dividing

proposedGroups.reason: The target defines the rate calculation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the special frontage assessment rate is calculated from the owners’ portion of cost and total metre frontage.

reason: The section addresses liability of abutting parcels and treatment of exempt parcels.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Abutting parcel liability for special frontage assessment
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address parcel liability and exempt parcel treatment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which abutting parcels are liable for special frontage assessment and how exempt parcels are treated on the roll.

reason: The section states a single clerk duty to prepare a local improvement assessment roll.

evidenceText: the clerk shall cause to be prepared a special assessment roll

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a focused roll-preparation duty.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the clerk prepares the local improvement assessment roll when a special frontage assessment is made.

reason: The section covers required notice contents and delivery methods for special frontage assessments.

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the ninety-day notice, required contents, and delivery.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the timing, contents, and delivery methods for notices of special frontage assessment.

reason: Section 136 separates the revision petition and clerk alteration process from notice of the clerk’s decision.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify petitioners, revision matters, clerk review, and alterations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may seek revision of a local improvement assessment roll and how the clerk handles errors, reductions, and intended frontage changes.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require notice to the applicant and affected owners and specify delivery.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who receives notice of the clerk’s revision decision and how that notice may be delivered.

reason: The section covers appeal rights and applicable court rules for revision decisions.

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address appeal eligibility, timing, and Court of Queen’s Bench rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may appeal a local improvement assessment roll revision decision, the fourteen-day deadline, and the applicable court rules.

reason: The section is a focused annual warrant of assessment rule.

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the annual resolution, warrant, and execution under seal.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how council annually determines the owners’ portion of completed work and executes the warrant of assessment.
